docs.acceptor.component: `Acceptor` is what makes a container a ZONE: it answers whether an element may enter.
The rule is DATA (`AcceptRule`), read by a pure machine — never a callback stashed on the
node. A container with no `Acceptor` is not a zone at all: it accepts nobody, rather than
throwing. What `occupied` does with a sitter already there is a separate question, answered
by `Displacer` — `Acceptor` is silent about who is already inside.
No rule stated means the default empty `and: []`, which the algebra reads as allow-everything —
a bare `Acceptor` is the open door, and a zone narrows by SETTING a rule. No atom at all is the
other extreme: judged by nobody, so nobody gets in.
docs.acceptor.zones: The LEFT area is a plain container — no `Acceptor`, so a card let go over it always bounces
home. The RIGHT one wears the atom with the rule you pick: the open door, or a capacity read
off the zone's own child count. Set the capacity to 0 and even the first drop is refused.
